part3.title: Part 3 – Complete the Story
part3.instruction: Read the story. Choose a word from the box. Write the correct word next to numbers 1–5. There is one example.
part3.storyText: Jane loves reading about different animals in her school [example: library]. Last Friday, Jane's teacher told the class to find pictures of animals on the Internet. 'Look on the (1) ________ I told you about yesterday,' she said. 'Work with a friend. Choose a really strong animal, but talk about your different (2) ________ first before you decide.' Jane worked with Paul. 'Bears are great,' Paul said. 'Let's find a picture of a bear standing in a cold river. They are really good at catching slippery fish with their big paws! Or how about a lion? People are really (3) ________ of those because of their sharp teeth and loud roar!' 'What about kangaroos?' Jane said enthusiastically. 'They have longer and much stronger tails than bears or lions. It's their powerful tails that make them brilliant at (4) ________ across the Australian outback! Their huge back legs are the strongest of all.' Paul turned to look at Jane in admiration. 'OK! You're right again, Jane!' he said. 'You're definitely the (5) ________ girl in the whole class!'

part4.title: Part 4 – Factual Text
part4.instruction: Read the text. Choose the right words and write them on the lines.
paragraphs: Dolphins are part of the whale family. They are much smaller (1) ________ most whales and they have small, sharp teeth which they use to catch fish.
Dolphins are extremely clever animals. They learn new things very (2) ________ and can make a wide variety of noises and clicks to 'talk' and communicate with other dolphins in their group.
Dolphins live together with their families in groups called pods. They absolutely love to play in the water and to jump (3) ________ of the waves and splash back in again.

A lot of people (4) ________ sail boats across the ocean say that dolphins enjoy being near humans. The friendly dolphins often swim very close to boats and sometimes they (5) ________ alongside the boats for many days without stopping.
Scientists study dolphins because they are so intelligent. They can even recognise themselves in a mirror, which very (6) ________ animals in the world are able to do.

part5.title: Part 5 – Complete Sentences about the Story
part5.instruction: Look at the pictures and read the story. Write 1, 2 or 3 words to complete the sentences about the story. You can use words from the story.

storyPassages.text: Daisy's family lived in a flat in the centre of the city, but every single weekend they drove to the countryside to visit Daisy's grandparents. They lived on a large farm. In the car, last Saturday morning, the whole family talked about what they were going to do at the farm. 'It is so wonderfully quiet there!' Daisy's mum said happily. 'I love working outside in the fresh air,' her father added. 'I love helping Grandpa look after all the animals,' Daisy said with a big smile. 'Look! Here we are at last!'

They were very surprised when they arrived and saw six enormous, noisy trucks parked on the farm. And when they stepped out of the car, it started to rain heavily. It was very cold, too. 'Oh dear!' said Daisy's mum unhappily. 'It's so noisy here today with all those trucks.' 'And I certainly can't work outside in this terrible rain,' Daisy's father complained. 'Well, you two should go inside and sit down and have a nice cup of hot tea with Grandma,' said Daisy firmly. 'But I absolutely have to go and help Grandpa feed the cows and wash the sheep!'

Daisy worked very hard all afternoon outside in the cold and wet weather without complaining once. She gave the hungry cows their dry hay, carefully washed several muddy sheep, and carried heavy baskets of fresh vegetables from the garden to the barn. After a delicious dinner that evening, Daisy felt very tired but also extremely happy and proud. 'The best and hardest-working farmer in your whole family is not your dad or even your mum. It is definitely you, Daisy!' her grandfather said proudly. 'That is so good to hear, Grandpa, because I really want to be a farmer just like you one day!' Daisy answered with a huge smile.
